text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.3% today to $141.22, driven by a sharp rise in global oil prices following geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Over the weekend, Iran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, forcing a temporary closure and prompting Saudi Arabia to cancel some crude shipments. Though world oil prices have eased slightly from yesterday's spike above $105, they remain elevated at $109.51 per barrel—well above the U.S. benchmark of $97.26—creating a favorable pricing environment for a major oil producer like ConocoPhillips.

The stock has climbed 6.6% over the past two weeks as these supply concerns have mounted, offsetting some headwinds from rising U.S. crude inventories reported today. Energy stocks tend to benefit when geopolitical risk pushes global oil prices higher, even if the disruptions are expected to be temporary; the wider gap between world and U.S. oil prices also typically benefits exporters.
